items.text: ## Local Development (docker-compose.yml)
Local development environment is defined in the file docker-compose.yml
docker-compose.yml uses compose file version: '3.8'
docker-compose service: postgres
postgres service image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
Local dev database: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector (image pgvector/pgvector:pg16)
postgres service environment POSTGRES_USER: postgres
postgres service environment POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres_dev_password
postgres service environment POSTGRES_DB: marketplace_os
postgres service port mapping "5432:5432"
postgres service volume pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
docker-compose service: redis
redis service image: redis:7-alpine
redis service port mapping "6379:6379"
docker-compose service: minio
minio service image: minio/minio:latest
minio service command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
minio service environment MINIO_ROOT_USER: minioadmin
minio service environment MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: minioadmin_dev_password
minio service port mapping "9000:9000"
minio service port mapping "9001:9001"
minio service volume miniodata:/data
docker-compose named volume: pgdata
docker-compose named volume: miniodata
## Core Environment Variables
Core environment variables are listed in the file .env.example
Env var DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://postgres:password@localhost:5432/marketplace_os
DATABASE_URL uses the postgresql+asyncpg driver scheme
Env var REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
The application connects to Redis via env var REDIS_URL (redis://localhost:6379/0)
Env var GCS_BUCKET_IMAGES=ai-marketplace-images-staging
Product images are stored in a GCS bucket (GCS_BUCKET_IMAGES)
Env var GCS_BUCKET_CSV=ai-marketplace-csv-staging
CSV uploads are stored in a GCS bucket (GCS_BUCKET_CSV)
Env var JWT_SECRET=super_secret_jwt_key_here
Auth uses JWT with a shared secret from env var JWT_SECRET
Env var LLM_API_KEY=your_hosted_llm_api_key
LLM access is through a hosted LLM API (LLM_API_KEY)
Env var LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT=your-preferred-fast-model
Default LLM model (LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT) is a preferred fast model
Env var EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small
Embedding model: text-embedding-3-small
Env var AMAZON_CLIENT_ID=amzn1.application-oa2-client.xxx
Env var AMAZON_CLIENT_SECRET=xxx
Env var FLIPKART_CLIENT_ID=fk_client_xxx
Env var FLIPKART_CLIENT_SECRET=xxx
Env var SENTRY_DSN=https://xxx@sentry.io/xxx
Error tracking uses Sentry (SENTRY_DSN)
Env var OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317
Telemetry is exported via OpenTelemetry OTLP (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, local port 4317)
## Git Workflow & ADR Process
Git workflow: Trunk-Based Strategy
Short-lived feature branches branch from `main`
Feature branches are merged via PR after CI checks pass
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits
Conventional Commit type: `feat:`
Conventional Commit type: `fix:`
Conventional Commit type: `chore:`
Conventional Commit type: `docs:`
Conventional Commit type: `refactor:`
Every non-trivial design decision is documented in an Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
ADR file path format: `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md`
## Indicative Infrastructure Costs
Estimated MVP Monthly Operating Cost
MVP infrastructure includes Cloud SQL (db-custom-1-3840)
MVP infrastructure includes Memorystore Basic (1GB)
MVP infrastructure includes Cloud Run (pay-per-use at low volume)
MVP infrastructure includes GCS storage
Estimated MVP monthly operating cost: Cloud SQL, Memorystore, Cloud Run and GCS storage combined land at approximately $150 to $250 USD/month
LLM API spend is volume-variable
LLM API spend is strictly monitored via `agent_runs` telemetry

# [1] System Overview
- **Section**: Overview
Page [1] System Overview scope: MVP
- **URL**: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/system-overview
The platform is an AI-powered marketplace listing operator for D2C brands
The platform has a four-layer architecture
- **Keywords**: system overview, marketplace OS, listing agent, D2C, four layer, ...
## What Is It
The AI Marketplace OS is an AI-powered marketplace listing operator for D2C brands
Brands create product listings through the platform
Brands validate product listings through the platform
Brands publish product listings across multiple marketplaces through a single interface
AI assistance is provided at every step of create, validate and publish
AI-generated listing content per marketplace: titles
AI-generated listing content per marketplace: bullet points
AI-generated listing content per marketplace: descriptions
AI-generated listing content per marketplace: keywords
AI-generated listing content per marketplace: attributes
Specialized AI agents generate marketplace-optimized content instead of manual writing and reformatting per platform rules
Generated content preserves the brand's voice
Generated content ensures compliance with each marketplace's specific requirements
MVP marketplace: Amazon
MVP marketplace: Flipkart
Two adapters (Amazon, Flipkart) prove the adapter pattern generalizes
AI Agents: 6 Specialized
Specialized AI agent: Content
Specialized AI agent: Keyword
Specialized AI agent: Attribute
Specialized AI agent: Image
Specialized AI agent: Brand Voice
Specialized AI agent: Optimization
Architecture: 4-Layer Platform
Layer order: Experience → Intelligence → Control → Execution
Data Model: Canonical + Adapters
Data model: marketplace-independent core
Data model: marketplace-specific mapping (Canonical + Adapters)
## Core Design Principle
Architectural Principle
Core design principle step 1: AI proposes
Core design principle step 2: Deterministic rules validate
Core design principle step 3: Humans approve
Core design principle step 4: Adapters execute
Core design principle step 5: Performance feeds back
AI is never given direct publish authority
Every AI-generated output passes through deterministic validation (Rules Engine) first
After Rules Engine validation, every AI-generated output goes to human review
Only after validation and human review does a marketplace adapter execute the publish operation
The core design principle (AI proposes → rules validate → humans approve → adapters execute → performance feeds back) is the foundation of the entire system
Safety: no hallucinated content reaches customers without human validation
Compliance: marketplace rules are enforced deterministically, not probabilistically
Trust: brands maintain full control over what goes live
Improvement: performance data feeds back to improve future generations
## Four-Layer Architecture
**Architecture Diagram: Four-Layer Platform Architecture**
```mermaid graph TB (diagram scaffold)

EXPERIENCE LAYER (EXP) component E2: Connect Marketplaces
EXPERIENCE LAYER (EXP) component E3: Import Products
EXPERIENCE LAYER (EXP) component E4: Review & Approve
EXPERIENCE LAYER (EXP) component E5: Analytics
INTELLIGENCE LAYER (subgraph INT) component I1: Content Agent
INTELLIGENCE LAYER (INT) component I2: Keyword Agent
INTELLIGENCE LAYER (INT) component I3: Attribute Agent
INTELLIGENCE LAYER (INT) component I4: Image Agent
INTELLIGENCE LAYER (INT) component I5: Brand Voice Retrieval
INTELLIGENCE LAYER (INT) component I6: Optimization Agent
CONTROL LAYER (subgraph CTR) component C1: Rules Engine
CONTROL LAYER (CTR) component C2: Structured Errors
CONTROL LAYER (CTR) component C3: Validation
CONTROL LAYER (CTR) component C4: Human Approval Gate
EXECUTION LAYER (subgraph EXE) component X1: Amazon SP-API Adapter
EXECUTION LAYER (EXE) component X2: Flipkart Seller API Adapter
EXECUTION LAYER (EXE) component X3: Canonical → Marketplace Mapping

Diagram edge INT --> CTR: Intelligence layer to Control layer

Next.js app covers: import

Intelligence layer uses LangGraph agents

## System Flow
The complete data flow from a brand entering the system to a listing appearing on a marketplace follows this path:
System flow step 1: Brand (D2C Owner)
System flow step 2: Marketplace Accounts (Amazon, Flipkart)
Marketplace Accounts in system flow: Amazon
Marketplace Accounts in system flow: Flipkart
System flow step 3: Product Catalog (CSV / Manual / Sync)
Product Catalog source: CSV
Product Catalog source: Manual
Product Catalog source: Sync
System flow step 4: Canonical Product Representation
System flow step 5: AI Context Assembly (Brand Voice + Rules + Category)
AI Context Assembly input: Brand Voice
AI Context Assembly input: Rules
AI Context Assembly input: Category
System flow step 6: AI Agents (Content + Keyword + Attribute + Image)
AI Agents in system flow: Content
AI Agents in system flow: Keyword
AI Agents in system flow: Attribute
AI Agents in system flow: Image
System flow step 7: Canonical Listing (JSON Schema)
Canonical Listing is defined as a JSON Schema
System flow step 8: Rules Engine (Deterministic Validation)
System flow step 9: Vision Validation (Image Compliance)
System flow step 10: Quality / Confidence Scoring
System flow step 11: Human Approval Gate
System flow step 12: Marketplace Adapter (Amazon SP-API / Flipkart)
Marketplace Adapter in system flow: Amazon SP-API
Marketplace Adapter in system flow: Flipkart
System flow step 13: Live Marketplace Listing
System flow step 14: Performance Data (CTR, Conversions, Returns)
Performance Data metric: CTR
Performance Data metric: Conversions
Performance Data metric: Returns
System flow step 15: Optimization Agent (Feedback Loop)
## Why This Architecture
### Why Separate Intelligence, Control, and Execution?
Intelligence (AI agents) is probabilistic
Intelligence (AI agents) can hallucinate
Intelligence (AI agents) can violate marketplace rules
Intelligence (AI agents) can drift from brand voice
Control (Rules Engine) is deterministic
Execution (Adapters) is marketplace-specific
Execution (Adapters) handles the complexity of each platform's API
Execution (Adapters) handles each platform's auth
Execution (Adapters) handles each platform's rate limits
Intelligence (AI agents) generates high-quality content
Control (Rules Engine) catches violations with certainty
Separating these concerns means:
AI models can be changed without touching marketplace logic
A new marketplace can be added without modifying AI agents
Rules can be updated without redeploying agents
Each layer can be tested independently
Each layer can be monitored independently
Each layer can be scaled independently
### Why AI Must Not Directly Publish
LLMs are powerful but non-deterministic
Amazon title limit: 200 characters (LLM may violate Amazon's 200-character limit)
A language model might include a medical claim that regulatory compliance forbids
A language model might use a competitor's trademarked term
Deterministic validation sits between AI and execution
Every character count is checked programmatically, not probabilistically
Banned terms are caught before they reach the marketplace
Category-specific attribute schemas are validated against known templates
Image compliance is verified through pixel analysis
Image compliance is verified through vision models
Architectural Invariant
AI never directly publishes data to any marketplace
The Rules Engine is deterministic
Human approval is required in MVP
These constraints (no AI publish, deterministic Rules Engine, human approval in MVP) are non-negotiable
## Non-Technical Explanation
Non-Technical Explanation
Non-technical view: an AI writing assistant, a strict quality checker, a human reviewer, and a publishing service work in sequence
The AI writes the listing content using the brand's voice
The quality checker catches any violations or errors using strict, programmable rules (not AI).
A human then reviews and approves.
Only after approval does the system push the listing to Amazon or Flipkart.
If the listing performs well, the system learns from that success for future listings
The AI writes the listing content using marketplace rules
## AI Implementation Context
AI Implementation Context
**What an AI coding agent must know before modifying this module:**
The four-layer separation is an architectural invariant; do not merge layers
All AI output must pass through the Rules Engine before human approval
The canonical listing model is marketplace-independent
Marketplace-specific logic lives exclusively in adapters
Performance data flows back to the Intelligence layer, not directly to Execution
**What this module must never do:**
Never allow AI agents to bypass the Control layer
Never put marketplace-specific fields in the canonical model
Never allow the Experience layer to call marketplace APIs directly
Never remove human approval in MVP

# [2] Architecture Principles
- **Section**: Overview
Page [2] Architecture Principles scope: MVP
- **URL**: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/architecture-principles
The foundational principles guide every architectural decision in the platform
These principles are invariants; they should never be violated
- **Keywords**: principles, invariants, rules, AI proposes, deterministic, human approval, adapter pattern
## Core Principles
Primary Principle
Primary principle: AI proposes → Deterministic rules validate → Humans approve → Adapters execute → Performance feeds back into optimization
Every system design decision must align with these principles
Principle 1: AI Is Advisory, Not Authoritative
AI agents generate content suggestions
They never have direct publish authority.
All AI output is treated as a proposal
All AI output must pass through deterministic validation before reaching any marketplace
All AI output must pass through human approval before reaching any marketplace
Principle 2: Deterministic Rules Are the Final Arbiter
The Rules Engine enforces marketplace constraints with certainty
No LLM output ships without passing the Rules Engine
Rules are programmable
Rules are versioned
Rules are marketplace-specific
Rules catch character limits
Rules catch banned terms
Rules catch missing attributes
Rules catch image specifications
Principle 3: Marketplace Independence via Canonical Model
The core listing representation is marketplace-agnostic
Amazon-specific fields live inside their respective adapter
Flipkart-specific formats live inside their respective adapter
Future marketplace requirements live inside their respective adapters
The canonical model never contains raw marketplace API structures
Principle 4: Adapter Pattern for Marketplace Operations
Every marketplace interaction happens through a well-defined adapter interface
Adding Myntra or Ajio later requires building a new adapter, not rewriting the core platform
Adapters own auth refresh
Adapters own rate limiting
Adapters own idempotency
Adapters own error mapping
Principle 5: Tenant Isolation Is Mandatory
Every database query is scoped to a tenant
Every API call is scoped to a tenant
Every agent run is scoped to a tenant
Cross-tenant data leakage is a critical security violation
Tenant filtering is enforced at the repository layer, not at the application layer
Principle 6: Structured Errors Everywhere
Every failure returns the same structured ErrorReport envelope
Rules engine failures return the ErrorReport envelope
Vision model failures return the ErrorReport envelope
Marketplace API failures return the ErrorReport envelope
The single ErrorReport contract enables AI correction agents
The single ErrorReport contract enables UI display
The single ErrorReport contract enables logging
The single ErrorReport contract enables retry logic
The single ErrorReport contract enables debugging
Principle 7: Bounded Retries
All retry loops are bounded
Retry loops for agent corrections: max 3
The system never enters infinite retry loops
Failed jobs surface exact reasons for human intervention
Principle 8: Observability by Default
Every AgentRun records: model_used
Every AgentRun records: tokens_in
Every AgentRun records: tokens_out
Every AgentRun records: cost
Every AgentRun records: duration
Every AgentRun records: status
Every marketplace call is logged
Every validation run is persisted
AgentRun records, call logs and validation runs create a complete audit trail
AgentRun records create cost observability
## Architectural Invariants
Never Violate These Rules (the architectural invariants below)
Invariant 1: AI never directly publishes to marketplaces
Invariant 2: Rules Engine is deterministic — never an LLM
Invariant 3: Human approval is required in MVP
Invariant 4: Marketplace-specific logic belongs inside adapters only
Invariant 5: Canonical listing model is marketplace-independent
Invariant 6: Tenant isolation is mandatory on every query
Invariant 7: Marketplace credentials are encrypted at rest
Credential encryption at rest uses AES-256
Invariant 8: All AgentRuns are observable and persisted
Invariant 9: All failures use structured ErrorReport contracts
Invariant 10: Retries are bounded (max 3 for agent corrections)
Invariant 11: Marketplace mutations are idempotent
Invariant 12: Failed fields are retried individually, not the entire listing
Invariant 13: Optimization Agent runs on schedule, not continuously
Invariant 14: Future marketplaces don't require rewriting the core system
## Why These Principles Matter
Reliability: LLM can never bypass the Rules Engine
Reliability: structured errors make every failure actionable
Defensibility: brand-voice vectors compound over time
Defensibility: version history compounds over time
Defensibility: performance feedback loop compounds over time
Marketplace independence: canonical model + adapters
Adding Myntra/Ajio later is an adapter, not a rewrite.
Cost efficiency: event-driven generation (only when needed)
Cost efficiency: model routing
The optimization agent only fires on schedule, not continuously.

# [3] Product Scope
- **Section**: Overview
Page [3] Product Scope scope: MVP
- **URL**: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/product-scope
Product Scope defines what the platform does and does not do: clear boundaries for MVP implementation versus future scope
- **Keywords**: scope, MVP, product, features, boundaries, what we build
## What the Platform Does
In MVP, the AI Marketplace OS enables D2C brands to manage product listings across multiple marketplaces from a single interface
MVP Connect: OAuth integration with Amazon (SP-API)
MVP Connect: OAuth integration with Flipkart (Seller API)
MVP Import: Bulk CSV upload for product data
MVP Import: manual entry for product data
MVP Import: catalog sync for product data
MVP Generate: AI generates optimized titles per marketplace
MVP Generate: AI generates optimized bullet points per marketplace
MVP Generate: AI generates optimized descriptions per marketplace
MVP Generate: AI generates optimized keywords per marketplace
MVP Generate: AI generates optimized attributes per marketplace
MVP Validate: deterministic rules engine checks compliance with marketplace requirements
MVP Validate: vision model checks compliance with marketplace requirements
MVP Approve: human review of listings
Human review option: approve
Human review option: reject
Human review option: edit
Human review option: regenerate
MVP Publish: push to marketplaces via adapters
MVP Publish: per-field result reporting
MVP Learn: performance metrics feed back for optimization
## What It Does NOT Do (MVP)
Not in MVP: Automated pricing intelligence (Future — Pricing Agent)
Not in MVP: Advertising management (Future — Ads Agent)
Not in MVP: Inventory management (Future — Inventory Agent)
Not in MVP: Returns optimization (Future — Returns Agent)
Not in MVP: Auto-publish without human approval (Phase 3 — confidence-based unlock)
Not in MVP: Competitive intelligence scraping (Phase 3)
Not in MVP: Myntra adapter (Future)
Not in MVP: Ajio adapter (Future)
Not in MVP: Meesho adapter (Future)
Not in MVP: Nykaa adapter (Future)
## Target Users
Table columns: User | Need | How the Platform Helps
Target user: D2C Brand Owners
D2C Brand Owners need: list products without mastering marketplace rules
For D2C Brand Owners: AI handles content generation
For D2C Brand Owners: rules handle compliance
Target user: Listing Operators / Catalog Teams
Listing Operators need speed for bulk uploads
Listing Operators need consistency for bulk uploads
Listing Operators need error reduction for bulk uploads
For Listing Operators: Bulk CSV import
For Listing Operators: parallel generation
For Listing Operators: per-row approval
Target user: Reviewers / Approvers
Reviewers / Approvers need trust before anything goes live
Reviewers / Approvers need auditability before anything goes live
Reviewers / Approvers need control before anything goes live
For Reviewers / Approvers: human approval gate
For Reviewers / Approvers: full audit trail

# [4] Users & Roles
- **Section**: Overview
Page [4] Users & Roles scope: MVP
- **URL**: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/users-roles
User roles and permissions follow an RBAC model
RBAC model includes maker-checker approval integrity
- **Keywords**: users, roles, RBAC, owner, operator, reviewer, admin, permissions
## Defined Roles
Table columns: Role | Capabilities | Restrictions
Role: Owner
Owner capability: Full access
Owner capability: connect marketplaces
Owner capability: import products
Owner capability: generate
Owner capability: approve
Owner capability: publish
Owner capability: manage team
Owner restrictions: None
Role: Operator
Operator capability: import products
Operator capability: trigger generation
Operator capability: edit listings
Operator restriction: cannot approve own generated listings (maker-checker)
Role: Reviewer
Reviewer capability: review listings
Reviewer capability: approve listings
Reviewer capability: reject listings
Reviewer capability: provide feedback
Reviewer restriction: cannot generate
Reviewer restriction: cannot import
Role: Admin
Admin capability: manage brand settings
Admin capability: manage marketplace connections
Admin capability: manage team roles
Admin restriction: operational actions only
Admin restriction: no data modification
## Maker-Checker Principle
Maker-Checker Rule
The generator cannot approve their own listing
Generator = the person or agent that triggered listing creation
Maker-checker prevents a single actor from pushing content to a live marketplace without oversight
Maker-checker is critical for compliance and trust
Even if a single person operates the platform, the system requires explicit review before publishing
Future: confidence-based auto-approval can relax maker-checker for listings that consistently pass validation
Confidence-based auto-approval only after a track record is established
